summary: IdP 'deviceid' claim emitted as JSON array prevents service-account impersonation for scheduled workers (private)
description:
Issue summary: Flowframe’s scheduled ingestion workers became unable to perform service-account impersonation after a tenant IdP rollout. Requests that previously succeeded now receive 403 during the token-exchange/impersonation step.

Impact: Scheduled background jobs (daily ingestion and model refresher) failing to create signed requests to Redwood APIs — customer reported missed data windows for two pipelines. Scope: affects one tenant (Flowframe) in their private VPC deployment in us-east.

Environment: Private control plane (v1.3.4), auth-proxy v1.3.4 deployed in customer-managed VPC, scheduled-workers running on customer's k8s cluster, IDP: Azure AD B2C via OIDC integration.

Observed behavior: During service-account impersonation (internal token exchange), the auth-proxy rejects the assertion with a 400/invalid_claims error and Redwood’s admin-api returns 403 for impersonation attempts. Audit shows the IdP 'deviceid' claim is an array (e.g. ["edge-host-12"]) while our impersonation codepaths expect a scalar string and perform claim canonicalization.

Expected behavior: Single-value claims emitted as single strings should be accepted and mapped to principal fields. If IdP returns array with one element, we should coerce to string for backwards compatibility.

Immediate customer-visible message: "Impersonation failed: mismatched claim type for 'deviceid'"
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private tenant with Azure AD OIDC where a custom 'deviceid' claim is emitted as a JSON array (single value array).
2) Configure scheduled worker to use tenant-scoped service-account impersonation for API requests (normal setup used by Flowframe).
3) Trigger a scheduled job that performs the impersonation flow and attempts to call admin-api to mint a delegated token.
4) Observe auth-proxy logs and admin-api response: impersonation step fails with 400/invalid_claims followed by 403 on downstream operations.
logs: auth-proxy[2026-03-13T08:12:09Z] WARN claim_normalizer.go:47 - claim 'deviceid' has unexpected type array; length=1; raw='["edge-host-12"]'
admin-api[2026-03-13T08:12:09Z] ERROR impersonation_handler.go:128 - impersonation denied: claim 'deviceid' expected string but got array
worker[2026-03-13T08:12:10Z] ERROR scheduled_runner.go:203 - job 'ingest-minute-metrics' failed: 403 Forbidden (impersonation denied)
comments: Aisha (support): Customer called in reporting daily jobs failed since IdP change last night. They confirmed the IdP started sending deviceid as an array after a configuration change.
Liam (eng): Reproduced locally with a test OIDC token. Auth-proxy current validator logs the array but rejects during type-assert. Will instrument further to capture raw assertion headers.

Flowframe (customer): We can temporarily switch jobs to use static service-account keys but prefer fix so impersonation stays tenant-scoped. We deployed IdP change to roll devices into group claim last night.
Liam (eng): Creating a small patch to coerce single-element arrays to strings in claim normalization. Will open PR and request fast-path patch release for private customers. Linked PR created.
investigation_notes: Confirmed token payload contains "deviceid": ["edge-host-12"] rather than "deviceid": "edge-host-12".
Auth-proxy schema validation currently treats arrays as multi-valued and rejects them for fields that map to routing/impersonation principals.
SCIM and role-mapper downstream expects string principal for device identity when computing service-account scoping rules; mismatch prevents building delegation context.
This first appeared after customer's IdP config change (changeset referenced in their ticket). No recent change in Redwood control plane for these codepaths prior to incident.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: support shipped auth-proxy patch (v1.3.5-rc1) that coerces single-element arrays to scalar strings during claim normalization. Customer applied patch to their private control plane and verified scheduled workers resumed normal operation.

Next steps: Backport patch to stable v1.3.x, add unit/integration tests for array->string coercion, update Claim Normalization Runbook, and add a config flag to opt-in strict type enforcement. Plan rollout to all private customers with advisory. Follow-up ticket INT-2046 tracks hardening and test coverage.
